correctness.summary: The median equation is reduced to an exact symmetric-beta probability deficit and the standard Bessel-K variance-gamma density. Small-argument expansions yield separate asymptotic balances for r<1, r=1, 1<r<3, r=3, and r>3. The scale conversion, beta second-order coefficient, r>3 cancellation, and both logarithmic critical coefficients were rechecked. The r=2 coefficient agrees with the known exact asymmetric-Laplace median, and direct numerical integration supports all five regimes.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Gaunt--Merkle (2021) posed the limiting median problem, Gaunt--Ouimet (2026) proved monotonicity and the limiting value, and Fischer--Gaunt--Sarantsev (2025) reviews the VG median and exact r=2 case. Searches across variance-gamma, generalized asymmetric Laplace/generalized Laplace, Bessel-function distribution, median/quantile asymptotics, large noise/scale/dispersion, and the critical values r=1 and r=3 did not locate the five-regime sharp rate expansion or its constants. The principal residual risk is older generalized asymmetric-Laplace literature, especially Kotz--Kozubowski--Podgorski (2001), whose full book text was not exhaustively inspected.

value.summary: The result turns a recently established limiting theorem into an explicit first-order phase diagram, identifies critical transitions at r=1 and r=3, and supplies practical asymptotic approximations with a nontrivial exact-case consistency check.

limitations: The asymptotics are pointwise for fixed r and theta.
No uniform crossover theorem near r=1 or r=3 is proved.
No explicit quantitative remainder bound is given.
The result treats variance-gamma laws, not general generalized-hyperbolic medians.
Older generalized asymmetric-Laplace literature remains a residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
